symptoms: The insects scrape the green parts from the leaf surface.
This feeding creates a pattern that looks like a ladder or a window.
These windows eventually dry up and fall out, leaving holes in the leaves.
In bad cases, the leaves become skeletonized and look like thin paper.
prevention: Pick off the insects by hand and destroy them.
Conserve natural enemies like wasps and bugs in your field.
Plant insectary plants like marigold or carrot to support natural enemies.
practices: Check your plants regularly for insects and eggs.
Collect damaged leaves that have grubs or egg masses and destroy them.
Shake the plants to knock the grubs, pupae, and adults onto the ground and destroy them.
